subject: Hypershift renewal — pricing & commit counterproposal
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@hypershift.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hypershift renewal — initial terms and questions

Hi Alice —

Hope you had a good weekend. We're starting the renewal conversation for HyperShift's account that comes up at the end of June. Before we get IT/procurement looped in, two quick asks so we can put a clean proposal together:

1) Can you share an updated 12-week forecast (burst patterns + expected monthly active endpoints)?
2) Are there any regulatory or KMS requirements we should include in the amendment?

Based on our usage snapshot, a few levers we can explore: a short-term price hold on the current per-token rate in exchange for an increased committed monthly token volume; limited bridge credits to smooth the initial ramp; and a conditional burst pool so you can exceed commit during product launches.

Attaching the recent usage extract so we're aligned on baseline (Hypershift_Q1_usage.csv). If you can send the forecast we’ll build two options: (A) 6-month price hold + 40% commit uplift with bridge credits, (B) 12-month modest commit with smaller discount.

Available for a 30-min call this week if that helps move faster.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

Attachments: Hypershift_Q1_usage.csv
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@hypershift.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@hypershift.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hypershift renewal — initial terms and questions

Thanks Marcus —

Appreciate the starter options. I've attached our forecast as requested (HS_forecast_May2026.xlsx). A couple of constraints on our side:

- FY26 budget is locked; we need predictability for at least the next two quarters. A price hold is very attractive.
- We'd prefer a shorter commitment runway but with a larger immediate uplift — thinking ~500k monthly token commit for 6 months.
- Bursts are mission-critical for our product launches; we need a firm burst-capacity guarantee (or explicit burst pool).

If you can do a 10% effective discount against our current blended rate plus bridge credits to offset ramp costs, we can move quickly and get contracts to procurement. Happy to take a quick call tomorrow morning.

Best,
Alice Wu
Head of Platform Ops, HyperShift
alice.wu@hypershift.ai

Attachment: HS_forecast_May2026.xlsx

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice —
> 
> Hope you had a good weekend. We're starting the renewal conversation...
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@hypershift.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Hypershift renewal — counterproposal (tiered commit + price hold)

Alice —

Thanks for the forecast — that's very helpful. We've discussed internally and propose the following counterproposal (high level):

Option 1 — Price Guard (recommended)
- 6-month price hold at current per-token blended rate if HyperShift commits to a 40% uplift over current average monthly usage (target: ~600k tokens/month).
- $150,000 bridge credit applied up front to offset first-quarter overage during ramp (applies only to usage billed against the new commit).
- Dedicated conditional burst pool: guaranteed capacity for up to 20% over commit during scheduled launches (must be booked 5 business days in advance).

Option 2 — Conservative Multi-month
- 12-month contract with 20% commit uplift, smaller bridge credit ($60,000), and price protection on the first 4 months.

Notes / Constraints
- Burst guarantees require a short SOW addendum (operational runbook + scheduled dates).
- Bridge credits are one-time and do not rollover.
- Legal needs to confirm KMS/retention addendum — Naomi will propose language.

Next steps
- If Option 1 looks reasonable, we can circulate a short amendment + SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.
- I'll also put a conditional route to Dedicated pool on the table if your team wants an isolated capacity plan.

I'll attach the counterproposal summary as a PDF for procurement review. If you want to tweak the price-hold length, call it out and we'll iterate.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

Attachment: counterproposal_20260519.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@hypershift.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hypershift renewal — contract path and compliance notes

Hi Alice / Marcus —

Following up from Marcus' counterproposal. A few legal/compliance items to smooth procurement: 

1) KMS/Key management: please confirm whether you require customer-managed keys (BYOK) or Redwood-managed KMS. If BYOK, we'll include an HSM integration addendum.
2) Data retention & logs: standard retention is 90 days for request logs unless we add extended logging (additional fee). Please confirm requirements.
3) Amendment path: attached is our short amendment-template.docx that covers price hold, bridge credit application, and burst booking process. If HyperShift signs that plus the SOW we can finalize quickly.

Operational note: if you plan to use Dedicated pool later this year, include that in the SOW so we can reserve capacity. Dedicated pool add-on requires a 60-day provisioning lead time.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with procurement/legal to review the amendment.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachment: amendment-template.docx
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@hypershift.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, contracts@hypershift.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hypershift renewal — pricing & commit counterproposal

Marcus / Naomi —

Thanks for the clear options. HyperShift is comfortable with the structure of Option 1 but with two small edits we need to confirm before sending to procurement: 

1) Price-hold length: we can accept a 6-month commit, but need the price hold to be 4 months (June–September) rather than 6 — trading stability now for flexibility.
2) Burst guarantees: instead of advance booking for every launch, can we have an unscheduled 10% emergency burst allowance per month (unbooked) in addition to the 20% scheduled burst? We'd accept a modest overage fee for emergency bursts.

If you can incorporate those points into the amendment and send a DocuSign envelope, we'll circulate to procurement and legal this afternoon. Attaching a signed statement of frontend intent (stub) so procurement knows we are committed to a fast turnaround.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll aim to finish signatures by next week.

Best,
Alice Wu
Head of Platform Ops, HyperShift
alice.wu@hypershift.ai

Attachment: signed_sof_stub.pdf
